planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Ken Aslet flowers and tuberizes somewhat earlier than typical mashua, holder of a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Ken Aslet is an intermediate-daylength mashua selection that flowers and tuberizes earlier in the season than the typical species, having arisen as a volunteer seedling at RHS Wisley in the 1950s and since earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit. Foliage is killed by any hard frost, but established tubers survive short freezes down to roughly 20-25°F under mulch. It is best suited to zone 9a or cool-summer climates like the Pacific Northwest, with tubers reaching harvestable size about 10 weeks after tuber initiation begins following the fall equinox.

planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Chilean Red is a vigorous, very productive mashua selection.

directions: Plant tubers in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Chilean Red is a fast-growing, very productive mashua selection with tubers colored yellow to deep red. Like other mashua it is a short-day plant, with tuberization triggered by shortening autumn daylength and harvest beginning in mid-November onward. It tolerates light freezes to about zone 7a with heavy mulch protection over winter, and the tubers mellow from a sharp, peppery raw flavor to a sweet, starchy taste similar to parsnip once cooked or frost-touched.

planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep in cool, moist soil after last frost; Humptulips is notable as one of the first seed-grown (true-seed) ulluco varieties ever commercially offered, since ulluco seed production is historically very difficult.

directions: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep in loose, moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Humptulips is a Cultivariable breeding-program release, documented on the Open Source Seed Initiative registry, and notable for being grown from true seed rather than only vegetative propagation, a genuine breakthrough for this historically seed-shy crop. It produces large, lumpy yellow tubers lightly marked with red at the eyes and deep yellow flesh, on a vigorous, drought-tolerant plant. Like other ulluco it needs a long, cool-summer season with tuberization beginning after the fall equinox, hardy only to about zone 9a.

planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep in cool, moist soil after last frost; Illimani is heat-intolerant above about 75-80°F, needing a genuinely cool-summer climate to thrive.

directions: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep in loose, moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Illimani is an ulluco selection with bright yellow tubers lightly speckled with pink, requiring steady irrigation through the growing season. It is heat-intolerant above roughly 75-80°F, so a genuinely cool-summer climate is necessary for good tuber set, which begins only after days shorten past the fall equinox. Harvest continues through winter as tubers size up, with cold hardiness to roughly zone 7a-9a under heavy mulch.

planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep after last frost; Hyak is a Cultivariable-bred, OSSI open-source oca cultivar introduced in 2016, selected for fewer but notably larger tubers.

directions: Plant tubers in loose, well-drained soil in full sun; Hyak is a Cultivariable-bred oca cultivar introduced in 2016 and released as an open-source variety through the Open Source Seed Initiative, selected for producing fewer but notably larger tubers (to 4.6 inches) for higher per-plant yield than typical oca lines. White skin with red eyes covers dense, firm white flesh that carries only slight tartness when cooked, giving it a texture closer to potato than the sharper tang of many other oca cultivars. Tuber initiation begins after the fall equinox, with foliage frost-tender but tubers surviving light freezes under mulch, reaching harvest in about 7-8 months from spring planting.

planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep after last frost; Black Oca is a prolific, high-yielding selection with distinctively dark tuber skin.

directions: Plant tubers in loose, well-drained soil in full sun; Black Oca is a prolific, high-yielding oca selection with dark red-to-nearly-black tuber skin, standing out visually from the more common cream, yellow, and pink oca lines. It follows the same day-length-driven tuberization pattern as other oca cultivars, with tubers bulking through fall and harvest following the first light frosts, which also helps mellow the characteristic tangy flavor. It is hardy to about zone 7a with heavy mulch protecting the tubers over winter.

planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep after last frost; Crema de Rosa carries a notably mild, non-acidic flavor, good eaten raw or cooked.

directions: Plant tubers in loose, well-drained soil in full sun; Crema de Rosa is an oca cultivar with cream-colored tubers blushed in pink-red, notable for a mild, non-acidic flavor that stands out from the more typically tangy oca lines and makes it good raw as well as cooked. Tubers bulk from the September equinox through November as days shorten, and the plant shows moderate drought tolerance once established. It is hardy to roughly zone 7a-9a with heavy mulch protecting the tubers over winter.

planting.note: Plant tubers 3-4 inches deep after last frost; Polar Bere's mild, sweet flavor (rather than the typical oca tang) makes it a good introductory variety for cooks new to this crop.

directions: Plant tubers in loose, well-drained soil in full sun; Polar Bere is an oca cultivar with pure bone-white to very pale yellow tubers carrying a mild, sweet flavor distinct from the sharper acidic tang typical of many oca lines, making it a gentle introduction to the crop for first-time growers. Tuber bulking is triggered by shortening fall daylength as with all oca, and the tubers are considerably more frost-tolerant than the foliage, which dies back at the first hard freeze. Hardy to roughly zone 7a-9a with heavy mulch over winter.
